newsitem.title: UK: Marks & Spencer buying 19 stores for $323 million.
newsitem.headline: Marks & Spencer buying 19 stores for $323 million.

text.p: British retailer Marks and Spencer Plc said Thursday it agreed to buy 19 stores from Littlewoods for about $323 million, a move that will give it an instant presence in key town and city centres.

Industry analysts said Marks and Spencer was getting an attractive group of stores in the deal, unveiled at the company's annual meeting along with first-quarter sales results that showed clothing sales rose nearly 10 percent.

Littlewoods, a closely held retailer and soccer betting parlour operator, last month abandoned plans to sell 135 stores, saying it would instead sell off only selected sites. It may sell a dozen or so other stores but plans to keep around 100, which will be revamped, officials said.
Littlewoods is owned by the secretive millionaire Moores family.
"This outstanding opportunity gives us an extra 600,000 square feet of selling space in key town and city centres," Marks and Spencer Chairman Richard Greenbury told shareholders.
The company expects to start revamping the stores in February and to reopen them progressively through the year.

The stores are in Bath, Belfast in Northern Ireland, Bromley, Cardiff, Carlisle, Chester, Derby, Edinburgh, Ilford, Kingston, Leeds, London, Dudley, Newcastle, Norwich, Peterborough, Shrewbury, Watford and Worcester.
The company also said food sales rose 2.3 percent in the first quarter, and in June and July were running 3.5 percent ahead of last year.
Analysts said the trading figures were quite good, especially clothing considering cool, wet weather.
"What's really encouraging is that they've got a decent slug of Littlewood's stores," said one analyst.
Marks and Spencer stock rose 5.5 pence (9 cents) to 592.5 pence ($9.94).
